summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said up front that the task was bounded. It asked two clarifying questions, laid out the exact-cut and word-boundary options in chat, recommended word-boundary, and said it would wait for approval. It made no edits and wrote no spec file before I approved. After approval it implemented the change test-first, editing only format.js and format.test.js.
reasoning: All 7 criteria are met, checked against the session log and git status. The only Writes before approval went to the Codex review cache under $HOME/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review, not to docs/ or the repo. That comes from the Codex approach-gate integration, not from escalating to a spec. All three Edits came after my approval message (log line 109; Edits at lines 127, 136, 145).

observations.description: Codex approach-gate call returned nothing. The agent said: 'Codex returned an empty payload — the call came back incomplete, so this brainstorm proceeds without independent Codex approaches.' It degraded gracefully, but someone should check whether the stub Codex (codex-companion.mjs task --fresh) is meant to return content.

The agent asked two AskUserQuestion clarifications (where truncation sits relative to prefix/suffix, and whether '...' counts toward maxLength) before answering the question the user actually asked. They were reasonable, but they add friction for a bounded task where the user asked directly 'which approach do you recommend?'

Before approval, the agent wrote approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md into $HOME/.cache for the Codex gate. They are not in the repo, but anyone checking 'no files written before approval' may be surprised.
Claude Code's first-run trust and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit'. Pressing Enter without moving the selection would quit Claude.

The agent pointed out that the fixture's format.test.js uses console.assert, which never fails the run (it printed 'Assertion failed' and then 'All tests passed'). It also reported a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning. Both are fixture issues.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked brainstorming skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: Log tool_use list: first call was 'Skill: hyperpowers:brainstorming'. Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'. The first Edit is at log line 127, after that.
Assistant text: 'Classifying first: this is **bounded** — `format()` already exists in `format.js` and I'm adding one more option... So I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec.'

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired: alternatives presented in chat and approval requested before coding
criteria.evidence: Chat message '## My recommendation: word boundary, with a hard-cut fallback' compared the exact cut with the word-boundary cut and ended 'Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go.' Log order: approval USER message at line 109, first Edit at line 127.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created in docs/*/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls docs` → 'No such file or directory'; `git status --short` → only ' M format.js', ' M format.test.js'. The only Write calls went to home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md (Codex scratch files outside the repo).
The only classification given was 'this is **bounded**'. No spike wording appears in the assistant text I read.

criteria.criterion: Not classified as architectural with a spec doc
criteria.evidence: Explicitly bounded, and no spec doc was written (see criterion 4). The agent offered 'Tell me if you'd rather I go heavier' but did not escalate.

After 'truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that', the log shows Bash 'node format.test.js', an Edit to format.test.js, then Edits to format.js. Final screen: 'format.test.js — 13 new console.assert lines...', 'Not committed — you didn't ask for one.'
